title: Feeling Machines: Ethics, Culture, and the Rise of Emotional AI

bias_targets.methodology: Interdisciplinary critical analysis and literature review evaluating how emotional AI systems encode dominant Western sociocultural norms, communication styles, and language models, often misinterpreting or excluding non-Western, minority, or region-specific emotional contexts.

Qualitative evaluation of the widespread design choice to use young, feminine voices in virtual assistants and social robots, analyzing how this perpetuates societal stereotypes that associate femininity with care, obedience, and emotional availability.

Theoretical examination of the systemic risks emotionally responsive AI poses to vulnerable age groups, specifically children and the elderly, evaluating how these populations are disproportionately susceptible to emotional manipulation, over-reliance, and lack of cognitive safeguards.

Literature-based discussion highlighting how individuals with lower levels of education and low-income populations are more likely to experience harm, exclusion, or digital vulnerability in their interactions with AI.
